A cathedral in Penonomé partially collapsed, and residents reported cracks in homes across Herrera province. Tsunami warnings were issued for Panama and neighboring countries. The US Geological Survey located the quake 10 kilometres deep, 10 kilometres southwest of Pitaloza Arriba. Panama's president reported no immediate deaths as emergency teams assessed the damage.
items.title: Strong 7.7 Earthquake Strikes Panama Causing Damage and Evacuations

items.summary: A 21-year-old woman identified as Jayda Allen Bonner was found dead in a Carlton apartment block. A homicide investigation is underway, though no charges have been laid and an arrested individual has been released. Ms Allen Bonner's aunt stated the family had been concerned for her safety and sought help from authorities. The incident remains under investigation.
items.title: 21-year-old Jayda Allen Bonner identified as woman found dead in Carlton apartment

items.summary: Ranjana Sengupta reviews Tahmima Anam's novel Uprising, describing it as a warning about environmental precarity and the abuse of women on a river delta island. The story follows Kusum Khan, a woman who leads an uprising against the brothel madam Amma. Sengupta notes the setting is tangible but critiques the characters as two-dimensional, calling the book a compelling, cautionary parable.
items.title: Review of Tahmima Anam's novel Uprising

items.summary: George Williamson, head of the Alan Turing Institute, warns that the UK must avoid dependence on foreign AI systems that could be switched off or restricted. Citing US and Chinese leadership in the field, he argues for developing domestic technology to ensure national resilience. Williamson notes that political and commercial pressures may limit access to AI in critical sectors like defence and healthcare. He emphasizes the need for sovereign control over technology to build an economy and maintain security without relying on external permission. The institute plans to focus on securing critical systems and producing smaller, nationally owned AI models.
items.title: Alan Turing Institute Head Warns UK Against Foreign AI Dependence

items.summary: Jon Davis presents a cartoon exploring the topic of job titles within the context of artificial intelligence. The item serves as a visual commentary on how evolving technology impacts professional nomenclature and roles in the modern workplace.
items.title: Jon Davis Discusses Job Titles in the Age of AI via Cartoon

items.summary: Three months after a wildfire scorched approximately 3,300 hectares in the Cairngorms National Park, drone pilot Pete Short and park staff conduct dawn patrols to locate smoldering hot spots hidden beneath the soil. Using thermal imaging, the team detects heat signatures invisible from the surface, guiding ground teams to extinguish remaining fires before they can reignite. While the landscape shows early signs of recovery, officials note that the full ecological impact remains uncertain. The drones are now programmed to fly repeated routes to monitor the site's regeneration over time and potentially detect future fires early.
items.title: Drones Hunt Hidden Fires Beneath Cairngorms After Wildfire

items.summary: A study by energy market specialists Guilherme Susteras and Alexandre Bueno warns that Brazil's planned opening of its free electricity market to low-voltage consumers raises significant credit and liquidity concerns. Based on data covering 88,000 consumer units and 1,400 shared solar plants, the researchers found a 17% average monthly payment delinquency rate and 4% customer churn. They caution that without stronger regulatory oversight, credit assessment, and liquidity management, retailers could face cash flow pressures, potentially leading to bankruptcies and higher prices for consumers. The study, developed by Allez Estratégia, highlights risks including information asymmetry and operational complexity as the market expands.
items.title: Study Warns Brazil's Retail Electricity Market Expansion Risks Credit and Liquidity Issues

items.summary: Indian police detained the head of the satirical "cockroach" online movement on Saturday. The group stated this occurred ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission, which prompted strict security measures. A correspondent provided further details on the situation.
items.title: Indian police detain satirical movement leader ahead of election protest

items.summary: An investigation by The Outlaw Ocean Project challenges the sustainability claims of Greece's aquaculture industry. While industry leaders promote fish farming as a solution to overfishing, the report finds that farmed species often consume wild fish, accelerating ocean depletion. The study highlights that Greek companies rely on fishmeal sourced from Western Sahara, an area occupied by Morocco, raising legal and ethical concerns. Additionally, the industry's growth is linked to environmental enforcement actions and human rights abuses globally. Despite these issues, the sector remains the fastest-growing food sector in the world, with significant economic value.
items.title: Investigation Exposes Hidden Costs of Greek Aquaculture

items.summary: Austria received 43,300 solar subsidy applications in ten minutes during its final funding round, surpassing the previous round's 24,900. The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism attributes this to high demand and plans to revise the system. Proposed changes include year-round applications, mandatory smart energy management, and a focus on European-made inverters starting in 2027.
items.title: Austria Sees Massive Solar Subsidy Rush, Plans System Overhaul

items.summary: NPR reporter Anas Baba documents one year of the Gaza ceasefire through photography, showing ongoing violence, displacement, and humanitarian struggles despite a formal truce. Images capture airstrikes, refugee camps, and moments of resilience across the region from late 2025 to early 2026.
items.title: NPR documents one year of ceasefire in Gaza with photos

items.summary: Residents of Whitted, Florida, report drinking water that turns brown and tastes like iced tea. Testing by the Florida Department of Health confirmed contamination with arsenic and PFAS in some wells. A $2.3 million project to connect the community to the city water system, announced in 2024, has not begun construction by 2026. The delay is attributed to bureaucracy by Osceola County Commissioner Ricky Booth. The site of a former landfill, which operated from 1964 to 1975, is believed to be the source of groundwater pollution. Residents, many of whom are Black, describe the situation as environmental racism and rely on expensive bottled water. The community seeks clean water and the transformation of the former dump site into a park.
items.title: Residents of Florida's Whitted Community Face Brown Water and Contaminated Wells

items.summary: Russian strikes on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia killed at least 12 people, including children, according to regional authorities. The attacks occurred as US, Ukrainian, and European officials met in Miami to discuss ending the war. While US President Donald Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia, Germany vowed to pursue new EU sanctions. In a separate incident, Ukrainian attacks on Russian-held Luhansk wounded five civilians. The Kremlin reported that Putin shared Iran's views with Trump regarding a potential resolution to the US-Iran conflict. Verification of some battlefield reports was not possible by Reuters.
items.title: Russian Strikes Kill 12 in Zaporizhzhia as Diplomatic Talks Continue

items.summary: French astronaut Sophie Adenot returned to Earth on Thursday after an eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station, breaking the record for the longest uninterrupted orbital stay by a European astronaut. Speaking in Cologne, she described experiencing the full range of human emotions and noted the physiological challenges of re-adapting to gravity following her 235 days in space.
items.title: French astronaut Sophie Adenot returns to Earth after record mission

items.summary: A women-led team in Chile's Patagonia National Park is releasing 13 Darwin's rheas in April 2026. Working with Rewilding Chile Foundation and Tompkins Conservation, the rangers face challenges like predators and fencing while aiming to restore the steppe ecosystem after a century of ranching.
items.title: Women-led team releases Darwin's rheas in Chilean Patagonia National Park

items.summary: Ring has announced a new smart lock featuring a hand-powered energy dial to generate electricity during power loss. This manual fallback allows users to unlock the door without a physical key if the battery dies. The device also supports fingerprint scanning, PIN codes, Alexa, and the Ring app. It is scheduled to launch in early 2027 for $250.
items.title: Ring Announces New Smart Lock with Manual Power Backup

items.summary: Shardiya Navratri 2026 is scheduled to begin on October 11 and conclude on October 20. This nine-day festival honors the nine forms of Goddess Durga through prayers, rituals, fasting, and vibrant celebrations. It is one of four Navratri observances held annually, alongside Chaitra Navratri and two Gupt Navratris, marking the triumph of good over evil.
items.title: Happy Navratri 2026: Celebrating Shardiya Navratri Wishes and Festival Details

items.summary: Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala announced that the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau will register an FIR in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case against opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan and others. This action follows a directive from the Kerala High Court, which the government stated it would honour without filing an appeal. Chennithala noted that the court ruled a preliminary inquiry unnecessary and that the verdict contradicted the CPI(M)'s previous legal arguments.
items.title: Kerala Home Minister Announces FIR Registration in CMRL-Exalogic Case

items.summary: On October 10, Delhi witnessed a severe security clampdown as police prevented a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against the chief election commissioner. The operation, involving around 35,000 personnel, escalated into mass arrests, with more than 3,000 people detained by late afternoon. Prominent figures, including CJP leaders, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, and opposition leaders Arvind Kejriwal and Mamata Banerjee, were among those detained. While the government defended the action as necessary to prevent unrest, opposition leaders accused authorities of suppressing dissent and curtailing constitutional rights. The day saw reported clashes, stone-pelting incidents, and significant disruptions to transport and internet services in the capital.
items.title: Delhi Police Crackdown on CJP Protest Escalates to Mass Arrests

items.summary: Police detained 'cockroach movement' leader Abhijeet Dipke and two others as hundreds of protesters defied a heavy security clampdown in New Delhi. The demonstration follows allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India. While the ECI rejected these claims, opposition parties argue the revision could disenfranchise millions. Authorities deployed tens of thousands of personnel to stop protesters from reaching the main site.
items.title: Police Detain 'Cockroach Movement' Leader Amid Delhi Protest Crackdown

items.summary: Former cricketers Sanjay Manjrekar and Danish Kaneria offered contrasting reactions to the CJP protest in Delhi. Kaneria urged Delhi Police to 'bat first' against demonstrators, while Manjrekar questioned the action, stating that peaceful protests are a democratic activity. The article notes that the protest was denied permission by police citing security reasons, and several leaders were detained.
items.title: Former Cricketers Clash Over Delhi Police Response to CJP Protest

items.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative elections to September 11, 2027, citing security and logistical obstacles, according to the Palestinian Wafa news agency. The move follows previous scheduling for November, drawing criticism from Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar and disappointment from the European Union, which had supported the original timeline. The Executive Committee of the Palestine Liberation Organisation approved the delay.
items.title: Palestinian President Abbas Postpones Legislative Elections to September 2027

items.summary: The BJP announced district-level agitations across Jammu and Kashmir, citing misgovernance and public grievances. Leader Sunil Sharma stated the party would confront the Omar Abdullah government outside the Assembly after being ignored. Activists protested in Jammu, burning an effigy of Rahul Gandhi and demanding his resignation. The opposition accused the Congress of creating anarchy and targeting constitutional authorities.
items.title: BJP Announces District-Wide Agitations in Jammu and Kashmir Over Alleged Misgovernance

items.summary: With local body elections approaching in Visakhapatnam, political parties are preparing custom campaign vehicles. Srinivas of SV Engineering Works reports receiving orders for various designs, ranging from open-stage vans to fully enclosed trucks equipped with LED screens and sound systems. Costs for these customized vehicles range from ₹3.5 lakh to ₹7 lakh, depending on the model and required facilities.
items.title: Political Parties Prepare Custom Campaign Vehicles in Visakhapatnam Ahead of Local Body Elections

items.summary: Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd. conducted bacteriological and chemical tests on drinking water at stations between Shiroor and Thokur. Additional chemical analysis occurred at Innanje and Nandikoor stations near a thermal power plant. According to a communique, samples collected from all tested stations were found to be fit for consumption. The tests aimed to verify water safety for passengers.
items.title: Konkan Railway Tests Drinking Water at Stations

items.summary: A Delhi court refused to cancel the interim bail of student activist Sharjeel Imam, who was accused of flouting bail conditions by allegedly interacting with media. Although the judge noted probable violations based on video evidence, the court declined to cancel the bail because Imam was already en route to surrender. The case involves charges related to the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.
items.title: Delhi Court Refuses to Cancel Bail for Sharjeel Imam Despite Alleged Violation

items.summary: Shiv Sena leader Aaditya Thackeray criticized the Election Commission and BJP-led government regarding the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. He stated that Gyanesh Kumar must go due to alleged voter omissions. Conversely, 124 former bureaucrats issued an open letter defending the commission, citing the 2025 Bihar elections where 22 lakh deceased and seven lakh duplicate voters were removed alongside 21.5 lakh new additions. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi visited Chennai for a student outreach event and met the Chief Minister.
items.title: Aaditya Thackeray Criticizes Election Commission Over Poll Bias

items.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party accused Delhi Police of forcibly detaining activists and dragging protesters attempting to reach Jantar Mantar. The party claimed over 7,000 people were detained while six police personnel were injured. Delhi Police denied the demonstration permission, citing late submission, and imposed security restrictions. Several leaders, including Arvind Kejriwal and Mamata Banerjee, were detained. The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized the protest as a 'flop show'.
items.title: CJP Accuses Delhi Police of Forcefully Detaining Protesters Over CEC Resignation Demand

items.summary: The Portuguese Football Federation provisionally suspended Cristiano Ronaldo and opened disciplinary proceedings after he walked out on the national team. Ronaldo apologized to supporters and criticized coach Jorge Jesus, stating he would accept any punishment. The federation classified the case as urgent while Ronaldo remains suspended pending a final decision on his penalty.
items.title: Portugal Suspends Ronaldo Over Team Walkout

items.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant intervened after the Supreme Court Bar Association sought help regarding detained advocates during CJP protests. He spoke to authorities, leading to their release, though he noted he was out of town. Police detained over a thousand protestors, including leaders and former chief ministers.
items.title: CJI Intervenes to Release Detained Lawyers Amid CJP Protests

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi met Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay at Vijay's residence in Chennai on Saturday. Sources cited by PTI state the leaders discussed political issues for about an hour. Following the meeting, they visited Bask by Coffee cafe in Neelankarai for talks over cappuccino and tiramisu. Vijay welcomed Gandhi with flowers. Gandhi is in Chennai for the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' student outreach program.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Meets Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay in Chennai

items.summary: The North Eastern Regional Power Committee convened to address urgent grid maintenance issues exacerbated by AI-driven demand. Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. reported that upgrading costs for supervisory systems rose from ₹521 crore to about ₹688 crore due to AI hardware expenses. Officials warn that data-centre projects, particularly in cities like Hyderabad and Mumbai, pose stability risks through rapid load fluctuations. While Alok Kumar of the All-India Discoms Association notes incremental demand remains manageable, transmission utilities face challenges in urban areas. The Central Electricity Authority and regional committees are studying these patterns, with Maharashtra officials suggesting line upgrades to 2,100 MVA to handle growing data-centre loads.
items.title: AI Data-Centres Strain India's Power Grid and Drive Up Upgrade Costs

items.summary: A California couple restored a historic backyard railway on a 1.55-acre estate in La Cañada Flintridge after purchasing it in 2008. The property, featuring a five-passenger train designed by Disney Imagineer Bill Tyson, sold for $8.5 million in 2025. Real estate agent Kathy Seuylemezian highlighted the unique rideable train as a standout feature alongside the mansion's amenities.
items.title: California Couple Restored Backyard Railway Before Estate Sold

items.summary: The Congress party plans to challenge the Madhya Pradesh High Court's order striking down 27 per cent OBC reservation in the Supreme Court. Leaders Jitu Patwari and Umang Singhar criticized the BJP government for failing to defend the policy adequately. The Congress remains committed to the quota if it forms the government after the 2028 Assembly polls.
items.title: Congress plans Supreme Court challenge over MP OBC quota verdict

items.summary: An article introduces key figures behind India's youth-led protest movement, which challenges alleged examination irregularities, unemployment, and electoral accountability. It profiles Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), and student leaders Neha Bora, Aishe Ghosh, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Ajinkya Shinde. The piece details their backgrounds, roles in organizations like CJP and JNUSU, and specific actions such as hunger strikes and legal challenges. It notes the movement's expansion to include opposition parties and civil society, calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged SIR irregularities. The text emphasizes how these individuals mobilize youth through street protests and social media.
items.title: Faces of India's Gen Z Protest Movement Highlighted

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke's family is unsure if he can attend his grandmother Savitribai Dipke's last rites after his detention by Delhi police. Savitribai, 85, died on Saturday at the family home in Hingoli district, Maharashtra, hours after Dipke was detained in New Delhi. The family has been unable to contact him. Dipke's father, Bhagwanrao, stated they could not reach Abhijeet and he may not return in time. His mother, Anita, expressed hope he would come but questioned his priorities. CJP media in-charge Vijay Mallangi alleged that party members and lawyers were denied access to Dipke. Bhagwanrao questioned the grounds for his son's detention, accusing authorities of targeting him for exposing alleged government corruption.
items.title: Family uncertain if detained activist can attend grandmother's funeral

items.summary: Portuguese media reported on Saturday that Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened regarding his departure from the national team camp. The 41-year-old left the squad in Copenhagen following a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus, whom he accused of breaking his word. While Ronaldo apologized for his actions, the FPF confirmed the suspension and urgent status of the proceedings.
items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Provisionally Suspended by Portuguese Football Federation Following Team Walkout

items.summary: Arsenal defeated Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, Oct 10, to resume the Premier League after an international break. Leeds took the lead in the 55th minute, but Bruno Guimaraes scored the winner in the 70th minute after coming off the bench. Arsenal climbed to second in the table on 15 points, while Leeds sits fifth on nine points.
items.title: Arsenal Rally to Beat Leeds with Guimaraes Winner

items.summary: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, recognizing her contributions to international justice and the global fight for accountability. The award highlights the importance of international law during a time of pressure on global legal institutions. Pillay, a former judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court, has championed the recognition of rape as a crime against humanity and served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. Her recent work includes investigating alleged genocide in Gaza and serving as a judge in the case against Myanmar. The timing of the award coincides with criticism of the ICC by the US and Israel, underscoring the need to defend international justice structures.
items.title: Navi Pillay Wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize Amid Global Legal Pressure

items.summary: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson expressed regret over a US-Russia agreement to supply diesel, citing energy revenues as vital funding for Russia's war of aggression. Kristersson reiterated Sweden's support for Ukraine and welcomed upcoming EU sanctions against 1,600 Russian military entities. Meanwhile, Trump and Putin discussed the deal, with Trump stating it would supply over 300,000 tons of diesel immediately.
items.title: Sweden Regrets US-Russia Diesel Deal Amid Ukraine War

items.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk warned of a hunger strike or foot march if Delhi protest leaders are not released by tomorrow. Meanwhile, actor Imran Khan was detained by Mumbai Police during a protest at August Kranti Maidan. The INDIA bloc plans a mega protest on October 12 against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.
items.title: Activist Sonam Wangchuk warns of hunger strike while actor Imran Khan detained in Mumbai

items.summary: South African billionaire Koos Bekker is facing opposition from Somerset residents regarding the expansion of his luxury hotel, the Newt. While the estate has created jobs and improved local infrastructure, critics cite concerns over pesticide use, water rights, and the renaming of a train station. Issues include flooding exacerbated by road building and the keeping of red squirrels in cages for guests. Although the hotel employs over 650 people and boasts spectacular gardens, locals argue the development prioritizes private interests over community needs and environmental stewardship.
items.title: South African billionaire faces local backlash over estate expansion

items.summary: Rune Energy is deploying modular data centers called RELIC to utilize excess solar power that grids cannot absorb. These self-contained units connect directly to direct current from solar arrays, bypassing conversion losses. Co-founder William Layden estimates 50,000 gigawatt hours of solar energy are wasted annually. While efficiency gains are limited, the primary advantage is reduced component costs and faster deployment. The company plans to scale operations to 100 megawatts of compute within 12 months, with current sites in California, Texas, and Massachusetts.
items.title: Rune Energy Deploys Modular Data Centers on Excess Solar Power

items.summary: Ethiopia is undertaking a massive environmental restoration effort, aiming to plant 50 billion seedlings by 2030 through the Green Legacy Initiative. This campaign seeks to reverse severe land degradation and deforestation that have eroded soil and reduced forest cover to less than 3 percent by 1989. While the government reports forest cover rising to 23.6 percent in 2023, experts note significant challenges, including low survival rates for planted trees and the compounding effects of climate change. Despite these hurdles, the initiative has mobilized millions of citizens and secured international recognition, positioning Ethiopia as a host for a future climate conference.
items.title: Ethiopia Launches Massive Reforestation Campaign Amid Climate Challenges

items.summary: BYD announced its 150,000th new energy commercial vehicle rolled off the assembly line in Huai'an, Jiangsu. The company reported selling 6,848 NEV trucks in September, a 113.33% increase. Through the first nine months of 2026, deliveries reached 53,032 units, up 28.46% from 2025. The Q3 model features an 800 hp dual-motor and 600 kWh battery.
items.title: BYD Reaches 150,000th Commercial EV Production Milestone

items.summary: Former DR Congo president Joseph Kabilla stated the country is in peril, claiming the situation has steadily worsened under current leadership. He criticized the government for prioritizing status quo over public welfare and accused President Félix Tshisekedi of refusing dialogue. Kabilla called for an inclusive national dialogue to restore democracy and peace, noting ongoing fighting continues despite mediation efforts by Washington and Doha.
items.title: Former DR Congo President Kabila Warns Nation of Political Crisis

items.summary: Hundreds of protesters were detained in Delhi during a demonstration by the Gen-Z led Cockroach Janta Party demanding electoral reforms. The group's founder, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained upon arrival in the capital along with other leaders. Delhi Police refused permission for the protest at Jantar Mantar and deployed tens of thousands of security personnel. The CJP accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of bias, a claim denied by the commission and the BJP. Despite heavy security, the group vowed to continue their movement.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party Leaders Detained During Delhi Protest Over Electoral Reforms

items.summary: Delhi Police detained thousands of protesters, including opposition leaders, journalists, and activists, ahead of a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protest, organized by the Cockroach Janta Party and student groups, was supported by various political organizations. Authorities imposed restrictions, including metro station closures, internet suspensions, and train cancellations, which organizers described as intimidation. Detentions occurred in Delhi, Mumbai, and Pune, with some journalists detained despite displaying press cards. The Supreme Court upheld the legality of the voter roll revision exercise, but concerns remain about its implementation.
items.title: Thousands Detained Across India Over Election Commission Protest

items.summary: Delhi Police informed detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke of his grandmother's death and offered assistance to travel to her funeral in Maharashtra. Dipke was arrested earlier at Delhi airport during mass detentions of over 1,000 protesters against the Chief Election Commissioner. Police sources stated it is now up to Dipke whether to continue protesting under detention or fly back for the last rites.
items.title: Delhi Police Offer Detained Protester Option to Travel Home After Grandmother's Death

items.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is proposing to expand a regulatory loophole that would allow certain toxic chemicals to be added directly to food without a safety review. Critics argue this expansion contradicts the agency's recent claims of closing loopholes, as it permits substances like perchlorate and phthalates at levels below 0.5 parts per billion. Advocates warn that these chemicals can cause harm at much lower doses and that the proposal ignores cumulative effects. The rule would exempt substances deemed to pose no appreciable risk, a definition critics say is flawed and unsupported by science regarding endocrine disruptors and neurotoxins.
items.title: FDA Proposes Expanding Toxic Chemical Loophole in Food
